fact: President Ruto said AI-powered risk engines were piloted in KRA's Customs Department alongside re-engineering of its processes.

Business Daily reports the Integrated Customs Management System (iCMS), adopted in October 2021, is Kenya's sole clearance system, where traders lodge import and export documents at Mombasa, JKIA and inland depots.
KRA Commissioner-General Humphrey Wattanga says KRA is upgrading and modernising iCMS from a back-end perspective, and is considering a move to the cloud.
Business Daily says iCMS involves submitting export or import documents into a single-window system.

Business Daily says under the EAC single customs territory, the importing country's revenue authority submits import documents electronically and the exporting country's authority issues a road manifest against them.

KRA says it has piloted all Customs modules on the integrated Customs Management System (iCMS) and from 6 May 2022 will no longer process entries lodged on Simba other than petroleum, ex-warehouse and CKD motorcycle entries.
Freight Logistics Magazine reports iCMS clears import and export cargo at JKIA, Moi and Eldoret airports, and KRA fully rolled out motor vehicle and bulk cargo clearance at Mombasa in November 2020.
Freight Logistics Magazine reports KenTrade's TradeNet is fully integrated with iCMS, with 35 partner government agencies registered and releases sent from TradeNet to iCMS automatically.

Kenya Revenue Authority says import declaration forms, sea manifests, bonds, cargo declarations and exemptions are submitted through iCMS at Mombasa, ICD Nairobi and border stations for cargo arriving or exiting from 7 July 2019.

KenTrade says its National Electronic Single Window System, a single entry point for lodging trade documents and paying fees, was upgraded and commissioned on 20 August 2021 with 43 stakeholder institutions onboarded.
